title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Nashandra began her life as a small fragment of Manus, Father of the Abyss. When Manus was defeated, he was reborn as many fragments varying in sizes. Nashandra was the incarnation of her "father's" want, and thus began desiring what she did not have: power.

Nashandra travelled to the land of Drangleic, and set her sights on its powerful ruler, King Vendrick. Deciding to seduce Vendrick, Nashandra assumed a human form of unparalleled beauty and warned him of a supposed looming threat beyond the sea: the Giants. She convinced him to invade the land of the giants to claim their power, which Vendrick did successfully. Vendrick then made Nashandra his queen, and under their leadership, Drangleic entered into a Dark-like peace. The rulership of Drangleic however, was not enough to quell Nashandra’s want, and she desired an even greater power: the First Flame, which she intended to claim for herself by using Vendrick and the Throne of Want.

title: Nashandra
snippet: When Drangleic was ravaged by the second war with the giants and the spread of the Undead Curse, Vendrick came to realize the true nature and identity of Nashandra, and what she had coveted all along. Knowing that his time was short and that his queen had to be stopped, Vendrick created several impasses that would prevent Nashandra from seizing the throne, and sealed himself away in the Undead Crypt. This left Nashandra the sole ruler of Drangleic, albeit without much left to rule at all, as the kingdom had been all but destroyed.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Once the Bearer of the Curse has finally cleared the way to the Throne and acquired the means to access it, Nashandra will intercept them and reveal her true form. She then declares the Bearer of the Curse worthy to assume her intended role for Vendrick, to have their power usurped by her so she can claim the throne for herself.

The Bearer of the Curse has grown too strong however, and Nashandra falls at their hand.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - trivia 
 trivia : According to the *Dark Souls II: Design Works* interview, Nashandra's design was inspired by Gravelord Nito's, and in the early versions of the story she was not meant to be the Final Boss, instead she had a role closer to Nito's from the first game. However, it is clarified that the two characters aren't directly linked.
**Her design also serves to link well with *Dark Souls II's* theme of "deep curse" - the world's curse of Undeath and the grim fate of the Undead to be chosen to perform an impossible task - that director Yu Tanimura wanted to draw out in the game.
In the Memory of the King, Vendrick refers to her under the shortened name "Shandra", likely his nickname for her.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: Manus at one point kidnapped Princess Dusk of Oolacile—possibly after her rescue from a Golden Crystal Golem—and imprisoned her deep within the Chasm of the Abyss. In the meantime, his prized pendant came under the possession of Seath the Scaleless and then a Chosen Undead in the future; Manus, driven by his unrelenting search for his pendant, snatched the Undead from the future and brought them into the old Oolacile. There, the Chosen Undead put down the corrupted Knight Artorias and journeyed within the Chasm of the Abyss, where they finally defeated Manus and put him to rest. While Dusk was rescued in the process, she was driven by Elizabeth into thinking that she was saved by Artorias, preserving the legacy of the Wolf Knight. Nevertheless, Dusk came to recognize the Chosen Undead's similarity to the fabled knight, and developed doubts of her own as to her true savior.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - description 
 description : A tall humanoid creature wielding a long scythe in her right hand. Her left hand emanates a purple light that can become an energy beam or cause an explosion when she puts it near her chest. Her legs are covered by a skirt made of a black goo filled with bones. She can also summon four black fountains that curse those who stand near them. She can speak and can change into a more human, yet still gigantic, form.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: Manus was a sorcerer of Oolacile, and after he died, his body was buried in the caverns beneath the city. 200 to 300 years prior to the journey of the Chosen Undead, the Primordial Serpent Kaathe arrived in Oolacile, in search of a potential Dark Lord following the flooding of New Londo. He manipulated the country to upturn the grave of the primordial man, Manus, buried beneath the dungeons of their city and resurrect him. Manus awakened to find his pendant missing, and was eventually driven into a beastly frenzy as his Dark Soul went wild, transforming him into the "Father of the Abyss".

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Although he was killed, the Dark Soul of Manus was so large and powerful that he was reborn in death, and his soul split into miniscule fragments that retained some will. These pieces began to coalesce once again by absorbing other humanities, becoming the incarnations of different emotions of Manus and then human in shape, with their own self-awareness: Elana was the embodiment of Manus' wrath, Alsanna of his fear, Nadalia of his solitude and Nashandra, the tiniest fragment of Manus, the embodiment of his want. These new entities had some recollection of their father and his dark powers and when the Abyss that they called home was dissipated they scattered across the land. To sustain themselves and seek power, they reached Drangleic where in one way or another they came into contact with the holders of magnificent souls, drawn to their awesome strength.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Manus was a primordial human who possessed an extraordinary soul consisting of a viscous, lukewarm lump of gentle humanity, an immense Dark Soul. He was also a sorcerer who used a rough and old wooden catalyst, very crude but large enough to be used as a weapon. His sorceries could grant a fleeting will to the Dark of humanity, induced to relentlessly chase enemies through channeling innate human affinities. Manus also possessed one half of an ancient stone pendant, a precious magical artifact that emanated a distinct, wrenching nostalgia as well as reverence.

title: Nashandra
snippet:

Obtaining the Kinship after the first boss fight will cause Nashandra to already be waiting inside the arena. The cutscene will also play in this manner if the player dies while fighting her, when reentering the arena after respawning.

title: Elana, the Squalid Queen
snippet:
Elana, the Squalid Queen -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Elana, the Squalid Queen, like Nashandra, was a fragment of Manus, Father of the Abyss, supposedly a fragment representing the trait of wrath. Regaining her form, she became Elana, and later wife of the Sunken King. It is unknown if she designed to betray the Sunken King or if she truly loved him, but one day Sir Yorgh and his Drakeblood Knights besieged Shulva, defeating the Sunken King and awakening Sinh, the Slumbering Dragon, who then let forth a toxic cloud which annihilated the whole city.

Somehow, Elana survived the siege, and became furious and vengeful for her city's destruction and possibly her husband's death. She took on her true form and now accompanies Sinh, accruing souls for the day of her vengeance.

title: Nashandra
snippet: Left without a king and with no means to claim the Throne of Want, Nashandra’s plans were stalled until the arrival of the Bearer of the Curse, an undead powerful enough to defeat the Four Old Ones and gain access to Drangleic Castle. Nashandra manipulated the Bearer of the Curse into opening the way to the Throne of Want by aiding them in seizing the Throne of Want. She directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Undead Crypt, suggesting that they put an end to the now-hollowed King Vendrick and claim his ring. She then directs the Bearer of the Curse to journey to Aldia's Keep to acquire the Ashen Mist Heart, and warns them that the Ancient Dragon there is no more than a prop and a false deity. At last, she directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Forest of Fallen Giants to visit the memories of the Giants and obtain the last key to the Throne: the Giant's Kinship.

title: Drangleic
snippet: drangleic_s_curses : At a certain point Nashandra, a woman of exceptional beauty, arrived in Drangleic from a foreign country, and entered Vendrick's good graces, becoming his consort. The woman warned the king of a country of Giants beyond the Northern Sea, creatures that possessed souls of immense power and that apparently presented an impending threat to his kingdom. Vendrick was himself interested in the strength of the Giants, which he coveted as a means to step closer to fire, to end the curse of Undeath. The king was seduced by Nashandra's words, and followed her advice to gather an army and cross the Northern Sea, in an effort to subjugate the Giants and claim their souls for himself. When Vendrick landed on the realm of the Giants, a brutal war ensued, where he slaughtered, pillaged and conducted every act of barbarism with Nashandra at his side. Once his army "triumphed" in subjugating his enemies, they returned to Drangleic with a number of captive Giants and an immense

title: Throne of Want
snippet:
At a certain moment during his reign, Nashandra came to Drangleic, she coveted the Throne of Want and the power of the First Flame, and seduced Vendrick in order to use him as a means to accomplish her goal, becoming his queen.

Much time later, after Drangleic was ravaged due to both the war with the Giants and the undead curse, which all of Vendrick’s and Aldia’s plans to cure were in vain, Vendrick found out about Nashandra's plan: to use the throne to claim the First Flame for herself. Vendrick reacted quickly and sent the Throne Watcher and the Throne Defender to guard the throne. He then fled to the Undead Crypt, where he eventually went Hollow, to keep his ring and soul from the wrong hands. He did all this in an attempt to stop Nashandra.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - lead 
 lead : **Nashandra** or **Queen Nashandra** is a boss and the main antagonist of *Dark Souls II*. She is fought at the end of the Throne of Want area, only after the player has obtained the Giant's Kinship; if the Throne Watcher and Defender have not already been defeated, Nashandra's boss fight will trigger automatically after theirs.

Although she is the final boss of the base game, the *Scholar of the First Sin* expansion added Aldia as a potential "true" final boss, whose battle triggers after Nashandra's if conditions are met. Prior to her boss fight, she appears as a special character in human form atop Drangleic Castle, where she can be talked to from afar.

title: Drangleic
snippet: In the darkest hour of his reign, Vendrick also realized that his Queen, Nashandra, was a creature of the Abyss, and harbored an insatiable desire for strength. She was a fragment of a dark creature taken a human form, obsessed with the King's powerful soul. Impelled by her cravings, Nashandra sought souls, and strove to make the strength of the Giants her own, everything to reach the Throne of Want and the link for the First Flame so it could spread the Dark. Her painting in the castle was in fact able to curse the undead, making them hollow and draining their life, and only the king knew whether the depiction of the Queen was a resentful mockery, or an affectionate exaltation. At this point Vendrick had achieved a profound understanding of the truths of the world. title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Nashandra specializes in dark magic and will immediately summon four Curse-inducing "fountains" once the battle starts. She has two methods of attack in addition to inflicting Curse on your character and eating away at their health:

**Scythe**: She will swing her scythe sideways one, two, or three times (the third having a slightly longer windup and dealing heavy stamina damage on block), or do an overhead swing with a long recovery time. Her scythe swings can easily stagger characters with low adaptability and poise. Rolling diagonally backwards is the most effective way at dodging both of these attacks when close to her.

title: Nadalia, Bride of Ash
snippet:
Nadalia, Bride of Ash -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Nadalia, like Elana and Nashandra, is a fragment of Manus after the latter was defeated by the Chosen Undead centuries beforehand. She came to Brume Tower in search of the Old Iron King, either out of genuine affection or to simply force his kingdom to crumble. But when she arrived, she found that the king had been slain, and his kingdom left in shambles.

Falling into despair, Nadalia split her soul apart and stored those fragments within various ashen idols throughout the hollowed and empty Brume Tower. Upon doing this, she erected a black fog that consumed the tower and brought back the deceased soldiers and warriors, bewitching them into defending her. Many knights of outside lands came to the tower to steal the stores of iron within Brume Tower, but Nadalia's idols both bewitched the ones who were willing to serve her, and destroyed the ones who would attempt to defy her.

title: Frozen Eleum Loyce
snippet: At some point Alsanna reached Eleum Loyce and became close to the Ivory King. She was in truth a fragment of the Dark Soul of Manus, Father of the Abyss, that, despite the fact that he had been killed centuries in the past, had retained some of his will and power. Alsanna was born as the incarnation of Manus' fears and despite being a frightened and frail thing she managed to to coalesce once again absorbing the other humanities, and then obtain the shape of a human, with her own self-awareness. To sustain herself and seek more power, she sought the holders of magnificent souls, drawn to their awesome strenght. Alsanna thus sought the Ivory King to sustain herself and smother her innate fear and was accepted by him, quietly finding a place at the side of the leader of Eleum Loyce where he provided her comfort and she accepted Eleum Loyce as her home.

snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - throne_of_want 
 throne_of_want : Below Drangleic Castle, the Throne of Want awaits. Here the Emerald Herald will meet the Bearer of the Curse one final time, declaring her journey completed. She warns that if the Bearer of the Curse proceeds, Nashandra, knowing the Bearer of the Curse will link the fire, and coveting the power of the First Flame and the Great Soul, will come for them. She urges the Bearer of the Curse to put an end to Nashandra.

After defeating the Throne Watcher and Defender, the Bearer of the Curse will be greeted by Nashandra, now in her true form, as a child of Manus, Father of the Abyss. The Bearer of the Curse defeats Nashandra.

title: Nahr Alma, God of Blood
snippet: The deity is associated with scythes, the same tool known to be emblematic of the mistress of the painting, as well as darkness, in a way that is reminiscent of the occult powers sealed away in Ariamis, of which the white crossbreed was permeated. The robes of Nahr Alma's followers are decorated with a white fur collar and bone-like protrusions that resemble wings without membranes. The small connection to magic and the power of the moon that the cult has through the Crescent Sickle could also be explained away by Priscilla's likely descent from Seath, who was likewise tied to the celestial object. Even the prominence of pyromancy among his followers could find an answer in this connection, as Pyromancers, of the Chaos variety specifically, often find their way to the frigid painted landscapes of the forsaken.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet:
Manus at one point kidnapped Princess Dusk of Oolacile and imprisoned her deep within the Chasm of the Abyss. His prized pendant eventually came under the possession of a Chosen Undead in the future; Manus, driven by his unrelenting search for his pendant, snatched the Undead from the future and brought them into the old Oolacile. There, the Chosen Undead encountered Knight Artorias, who had retained only the very last vestige of his sanity in the battle against the Abyss, still desperate to put down the corrupted creatures of Oolacile. During the fight that ensued between him and the Chosen Undead, Artorias succumbed to the Abyss entirely, and was finally defeated by the Undead.

Ciaran, who had arrived at the arena where Artorias was corrupted by the Abyss, also requested the Soul of Artorias from the Chosen Undead who had finally put an end to the knight's suffering, with the intention of paying proper respects to her passed dear friend.

title: Goddess Fina
snippet:
Goddess Fina -  Dark Souls III - character - theories 
 theories : The Goddess Fina may have some connection to the Fire Keepers, as Lautrec's mission was to slay Anastacia of Astora and take her soul for himself, presumably as an offering to his goddess. The reason why he wished to do so is never stated or elaborated upon.

It's possible that the Nehma, the Goddess of Love from *Dark Souls II*, is connected to Fina, maybe even being the name she was given by the people of Drangleic and its neighbors. While her domain is not fully established, love seems to be quite a big part of Fina's character, even if fickle by nature. This could be an extra point to her own connection to the Fire Keepers, as Nehma's symbol is that of the Estus Flask, and in the first *Dark Souls*, the souls of Fire Keepers would be used to strengthen their healing proprieties.

 war_with_drangleic : Giants are primarily known through their conflict with King Vendrick and his kingdom. According to legend, a mysterious woman named Nashandra, said to be of unparalleled beauty, came to Vendrick long ago and warned him of a looming threat across the seas, in the land of the Giants. King Vendrick named Nashandra his queen and crossed the ocean with her to combat the Giants. During this conflict, he pillaged the Giant's lands, and stole an unspecified "prize", which he brought back to Drangleic. Using this acquired power, Vendrick created various types of Golems, who in turn built Drangleic Castle.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Manus may be named for Mannus, the father of mankind in Germanic mythology. According to the Roman writer Tacitus, the Germanic tribes believed a god *Tuisto* sprang from the ground and had a son, *Mannus*, from whom all humans were descended. Manus is also the Latin word for “hand”, alluding to Manus’s massive left hand.
**However a more accurate translation of "深淵の主マヌス" would be "Manus, Lord of the Abyss".

title: Chosen Undead
snippet: Finally, the Chosen Undead arrives at the Chasm of the Abyss where an illusion of Alvina guides the player to an illusory wall. Inside, the Chosen Undead discovers an injured Sif, protected by a magic barrier created by Artorias, in order to prevent Sif from being engulfed. Shortly after rescuing Sif the player faces Manus, Father of the Abyss, who is responsible for the spread of the dark. Manus is defeated, and Princess Dusk is saved. Upon returning to Oolacile Sanctuary, they are greeted by Elizabeth, who tells the Chosen Undead that she will let everyone know that Artorias was the one who defeated Manus, so that his honor may prevail. snippet:

title: Dusk of Oolacile
snippet:
Dusk of Oolacile -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Dusk appears to believe that she was saved by Artorias, as told by the legend, while in actuality she was saved by the Chosen Undead. While unaware that Artorias had been corrupted by the Abyss before he could save her, Dusk's senses do hint that the Chosen Undead bears the same "resonance" as her fabled savior, leading her to question the details of her temporarily intangible captivity.
The feelings that she sensed during her imprisonment in the Abyss—"*a wrenching nostalgia, a lost joy, an object of obsession, and a sincere hope to reclaim it"—*are evocative of the "shards" of Manus present in Drangleic, who each represented a form of longing; namely Nadalia, Alsanna, Nashandra and Elana.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: As the Abyss spread across the land of Oolacile, Knight Artorias arrived to halt its advance and confront Manus, as the Knight of Gwyn already had experience with fighting the Abyss and its creatures after the events of New Londo and his hunt for the Darkwraiths, and possessed a Silver Pendant that protected him from the Dark. However, Artorias's pendant was stolen by Oolacile's inhabitants and hidden behind an illusory wall, depriving Artorias of protection against Manus's dark sorceries. Together with his trusted companion Sif, Artorias faced Manus but his strength proved insufficient to defeat him, and he succumbed to the Abyss. Injured in the battle, Artorias used his Cleansing Greatshield to form a magic barrier that protected Sif from the Dark. Now corrupted to his soul by the Abyss and with his armor corroded, Artorias was left to fight alone and hold back the treacherous citizens of Oolacile.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
If the player wishes to face Manus conventionally, it is advisable to equip stamina-boosting items that such as the Cloranthy Ring, as well as a high-Stability shield that blocks physical damage. Only attack Manus after he finishes his jumping smash or frenzy combo, lest you be caught in the middle of his strikes.

Manus will start using his magic attacks at around 50% health. Use the Silver Pendant to deflect them, as they are difficult to dodge.

title: Mytha, the Baneful Queen
snippet: She was engaged with the Prince of Alken, but he had no affection for her in spite of her beauty and had a secret love for the Princess of Venn. The knowledge of this drove her mad, causing her to enslave the people of her land; Mytha relied on Mounted Overseers and Manikins to control her slaves, and also hired Desert Sorceress of Jugo to lure more people in her domain. She also hired Mirrah's Suspicious Shadows and the Undead Crypt's Grave Wardens to help keep order. The slaves were to dig the land of Harvest Valley, allowing her to consume the poisonous substances that sprouded from the earth, which would supposedly increase her beauty. Instead, the substances only corrupted her and transformed her into a reptilian monster. The frustration of not only failing to obtain more beauty, instead turning into a monster, prompted her to behead all her Manikins.

title: Mytha, the Baneful Queen

title: Mytha, the Baneful Queen
snippet:
The presence of Artificial Undead implies that Mytha operated in cahoots with the Skeleton Lords, and probably she uncovered their actions from her husband in exchange of some of their creations.

A man that is believed to have loved her followed alongside. However, as she was oblivious to the affections of any other man that was not the king, his feelings were ignored. That man is said to have transformed into the monster known as the Covetous Demon.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - notes 
 notes : The Silver Pendant, although not required, can be of great help as it blocks his magic attacks if used with correct timing.

Great Grey Wolf Sif can help in this battle. Whilst Sif's attacks are not very damaging, the extra summon can keep Manus distracted and give the player time to heal. It is wise to only summon Sif after Manus is below half health, to distract him in his harder phase, making it less likely the player will be targeted by the Dark Orb barrage attack.

Sif's summon sign is *inside* the Manus's arena, directly to the left of where the player spawns. As a result, Sif can only be summoned *during* the fight. Thankfully, Sif is summoned instantly after touching the sign, without the usual white phantom-summoning animation. Since it is summoned during the fight it does not increase Manus' Hp.

title: Queen of Lothric
snippet:
Queen of Lothric -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : The Queen of Lothric was the latest matriarch of the titular kingdom. She was wed to King Oceiros, and likened to the goddess of fertility and bounty.

She delivered three scions to the royal bloodline during her time as queen. The first of them was Lorian, a boy raised to be a knight, who grew up into a hero and found glory battling the Demons and defeating their Prince in combat. The second one was Lothric, a sickly boy born to be a Lord of Cinder, left for High Priestess Emma to raise. The last one was Ocelotte, a mysterious child of dragons whose birth caused the Queen's equally mysterious disappearance.

These were not her only children, however. The Queen of Lothric had a holy maiden who was also her direct offspring, while sharing no blood relation with Lothric's royal family. Whether she had the child before her marriage with Oceiros or during it is not clarified.

title: Queen of Lothric
snippet: Analyzing the Queen of Lothric's behavior also shows very little overlap with that of the Gwynevere established within the same game. The Princess of Sunlight is characterized as a kind, loving figure who was cherished and adored in turn. A great mother who raised each of her children with love, remembered fondly to the very end. In contrast, the Queen of Lothric willingly married into a family bent on creating the perfect sacrifice and eager to do anything in order to achieve that. She gave life to Lothric just so he may one day be used as kindling, without even raising him herself but handing him off to a wet nurse instead. She did nothing when her own daughter was imprisoned and left to wither away in a cell, and also abandoned her newborn son with her maddened husband.

title: Nehma, Goddess of Love
snippet:
Nehma, Goddess of Love -  Dark Souls II - character - theories 
 theories : It's possible that Nehma is connected to the Goddess Fina, maybe even being the name she was given by the people of Drangleic and its neighbors. While her domain is not fully established, love seems to be quite a big part of Fina's character, even if fickle by nature.

Another possible connection to Fina is through the Estus Flask, the symbol of Nehma. In *Dark Souls*, Estus Flasks were enhanched using Fire Keeper Souls, and Knigh Lautrec's mission involved killing the Fire Keeper in Firelink Shrine and presumably taking her soul to his goddess.

title: Drangleic
snippet: and conducted every act of barbarism with Nashandra at his side. Once his army "triumphed" in subjugating his enemies, they returned to Drangleic with a number of captive Giants and an immense number of souls as their prize.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: Kaathe, following his failure with the Four Kings, arrived in Oolacile and manipulated its inhabitants into upturning the grave of Manus, a primordial man with an extraordinary Dark Soul and dark sorcery skills, who had been buried beneath the dungeons of their city, and resurrect him. Awakening to find his precious broken pendant missing, Manus was eventually driven mad and his Dark Soul went wild, transforming him into a dark beast eternally seeking his pendant. His immense mass of humanity out of control led to the manifestation of an Abyss that spread, threatening to devour the entire land. The Dark emanating from Manus not only generated countless Humanity Phantoms with a will of their own but also influenced the residents of Oolacile, making their humanity go wild and horribly mutating their bodies, bloating their head and opening them with cracks lined with innumerable tiny red eyeballs and protruding brain parts.

title: Nehma, Goddess of Love
snippet:
Nehma, Goddess of Love -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Nehma is the goddess of love, though we are not told much else about her other than this. Unlike most gods, there are no mentions of Nehma in-game, and the Name-engraved Ring is the only item to assert her existence.

Her symbol is an Estus Flask.

title: Man Serpent (Lore)
snippet: Ultimately, they might simply be the result of various experiments related to dragons or the Man Serpents, either conducted by Seath himself, who wasn't unfamiliar with merging two different beings together to further his research as evidenced by the existence of Manscorpion Tark and Scorpioness Najka, or by the Bastille Lord himself, their former master.

title: Emerald Herald
snippet: Royal Sorcerer Navlaan tells the player many people believe the Emerald Herald is the last firekeeper. Navlaan will also say she is sometimes known as the "Muse".

title: Scorpioness Najka
snippet:
Scorpioness Najka -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Najka and her betrothed, Manscorpion Tark, were created long ago by an unnamed master who has long since disappeared. It is implied that the two were experiments, and that their creator was either Seath the Scaleless himself.

The two were once a peaceful couple living a quiet existence in the Shaded Ruins. But as time passed, Najka slowly began losing her mind and became more and more violent and unreasonable as a result. A war began between Tark and Najka, and has been waged for many years before the player's arrival.

title: Throne Watcher and Defender
snippet:
Throne Watcher and Defender -  Dark Souls II - boss - notes 
 notes : If the player has obtained the Giant's Kinship, then Nashandra will enter the arena immediately after this fight in a cinematic, and her boss fight will start. Any players or NPCs summoned that have survived the fight will remain with the host to defeat Nashandra and then Aldia.
The Throne Watcher is left-handed, unlike most bosses in the game.
By using a Bonfire Ascetic on the Drangleic Castle bonfire, King's Gate, Throne Watcher and Defender can be respawned.

This is likely due to the player having slain the Old Iron King and come to possess his soul.

title: Nadalia, Bride of Ash
snippet:
Sometime after his defeat at the hands of Velstadt, Sir Raime of Drangleic came to Brume Tower in search of greater power, and eventually came to view Nadalia as a mother figure. Rather than purge the black fog, Raime instead chose to live alongside the fog, and became Nadalia's loyal guardian.

Her original body can be found at the bottom of the tower past Raime, clutching the Crown of the Old Iron King and sitting upon his throne.

title: Emerald Herald
snippet:
Shanalotte will once again appear once the Bearer of the Curse has reached the Dragon Aerie. Here, she will reveal that it was her manifestations that led them here, and has been guiding them all along. She directs the Bearer to the top of the aerie, where the Ancient Dragon awaits them.

Shanalotte will appear one final time when the Bearer of the Curse is approaching the Throne of Want. She will tell the Bearer of her origins and her true name. She will warn them that Nashandra, desiring the power of the Flame and the Great Soul will come after them, but that they must persist nonetheless.

Should the Bearer of the Curse choose to claim the throne, Shanalotte will narrate their ascent, explaining that linking the flame will cause souls to flourish anew but that the events that have transpired will play out all over again, and that it is the Bearer's choice whether to embrace or renounce this.

title: Alsanna, Silent Oracle
snippet:
Alsanna, Silent Oracle -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Alsanna is a mysterious child of the Dark, one of the many fragments of Manus, Father of the Abyss. At an unknown point, she traveled to the northern kingdom of Eleum Loyce, ruled by the Ivory King, and devoted herself to him as his oracle. An ancient Chaos was discovered deep below the land, so in an attempt to appease the raging flame the Ivory King built a great cathedral at its mouth and Alsanna prayed in silent vigilance. The attempt was unsuccessful, and the flames still raged.

title: Spear of the Church
snippet: These holy warriors are all that stands between the Ashen One and the sleeping princess, who presumably held the key to obtaining the Dark Soul. Even the last of the Spears falls to them in time.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Thanks to this discovery Vendrick became the monarch who came closest to becoming a true "King" and turning his wants into reality. He had access to the primordial Flame whose power could decide the fate of the world, either by linking it to prolong the state of the world or refusing this fate and leading the world to darkness as a Dark Lord. Vendrick, however, never made either decision and continued to reign over Drangleic. Both he and his brother were not convinced by the two possible choices and, anchored to the illusion of the form that life had during the Age of Fire, they looked for a way to maintain it, searching for a way to free humans from the curse of Undeath and breaking the seal of fire that imprisoned them. As he deepened his knowledge of souls and curses, Vendrick effectively reigned over Drangleic, protecting the country from any external threats. Nashandra helped bring peace to the kingdom, a peace so profound that it reminded humans of the Dark from which they came.

title: Gods

title: Olaphis
snippet: In addition to the undead curse, the Northern Sea became infested by the Varangians, a group of sea-faring marine warriors. title: Northern Sea
snippet: During his reign, King Vendrick was advised by Queen Nashandra that across the sea there was the looming thretat of the Giants. Vendrick gathered an army and crossed the ocean, defeated the Giants, pillaged their land and took control of their great power, using it to create the golems and further develop his kingdom. However, the giants, angered by the invasion and barbarism of the king of Drangleic, responded by crossing the sea and directly invading the human kingdom with the desire to take revenge on Vendrick, bringing war that consumed Drangleic for centuries with their directed and burning rage..

snippet:
Nahr Alma, God of Blood -  Dark Souls II - character - trivia 
 trivia : Nahr Alma's Japanese name is "**ドロマ**", meaning "Doroma/Doloma". Interestingly enough, it appears to be similar to the name of a genus of moth.

The two gods are the figureheads of opposing covenants, so perhaps this is meant to highlight their rivalry, as one would be a moth and the other a butterfly.
Curiously enough, Titchy Gren, the only worshipper of Nahr Alma in-game, makes use of Caitha's Chime when casting his Hexes. It is unkown if he favors the chime because of its affinity to darkness, or if it implies some sort of connection between Nahr Alma and Goddess Caitha.

The king took with him only a handful of Royal Soldiers and the faithful Sir Velstadt, and found refuge in the Shrine of Amana. Vendrick was initially intent on reaching the Throne of Want and link the First Flame but in the end the king understood that if he did so, Nashandra would have gained an easy access to the throne connected to the Flame. Vendrick thus decided to free himself from his soul, abandoning it among the ruins, to descend even deeper into the Undead Crypt. Her friendship with Midir could also take on a new light, as if she had draconic descent, she'd be able to relate and even grow incredibly close to the great being with relative ease due to their partially shared roots.

Betrayed and filled with righteous fury, she attacks the Unkindled in the name of her heritage, her princess and her companion Midir. title: Princess of Venn
snippet:
In addition to that, both characters are women, and both of them are connected to the Lost Bastille; the Sinner for being imprisoned in the nearby Sinners' Rise, and the Princess of Venn for building her belfry within the old fort. The Queen of Venn wouldn't even need any direct relation to pyromancy herself, as while the Lost Sinner is connected to the Witch of Izalith and the art itself, she never uses any form of flame during her battle, instead relying only on incredibly skilled swordplay.

title: New Londo Ruins
snippet: Despite this, the residuals sins of these knights who had succumbed to the temptations of dark reached Drangleic in the form of Cracked Red Eye Orbs. These artifacts were actively employed by the covenant of the Brotherhood of Blood to invade other locations and times and collect the blood of other Undead. Although this cult followed the same combat and invasion philosophy as the original covenant of the Darkwraiths, it was also centered around the mysterious figure of the god Nahr Alma, God of Blood and encouraged its followers to reject the world and follow a path of constant struggle and bloodshed, indulging in their hedonistic desires for violence to collect blood and offer it as a sacrifice for their god instead of seeking to understand the Dark powers of the humans.

title: Nameless Blacksmith Deity
snippet:
Nameless Blacksmith Deity -  Dark Souls - character - about_their_place_in_the_world 
 about_their_place_in_the_world : It's possible that the Divine Blacksmiths were worshippers or even direct followers of the Nameless Blacksmith Deity, and that their statues depict them praying to the god.

As the gods' original blacksmith, it's also likely that they worked on or oversaw the production of many of the armors, weapons, and other various equipment used by the pantheon and their followers. The unique flower design featured on the armors of Smough, Gwyn, and even the Crystal General, could potentially be traced back to them, though it might just be a general symbol of the royal family of Anor Londo, in reference to the chrysanthemum being a symbol of the Japanese Imperial Family.

title: Royal Sorcerer Navlaan

If the Bearer of the Curse releases Navlaan, Navlaan will declare that he has found a new mark, and will begin relentlessly pursuing them.

title: Nadalia, Bride of Ash

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet: Ages after her Lord Soul was used to link the First Flame, Izalith's very name was lost. In the region of Drangleic, only few remained who remembered her—only that she was the mother of pyromancy, and that she was devoured by her chaos flame. However, some remnants of her soul manifested again in Drangleic, continuing to exert their influence on the region.

title: Corvian (Lore)
snippet:
Corvian (Lore) -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : By the time of Drangleic, knowledge of the Painted World had been lost. Regardless, some of its Corvian inhabitants took their leave, as one of their descendants, Weaponsmith Ornifex, can be found in the old town of Tseldora. Her choice to live in Tseldora seems rather curious, as the town has some passing connection to the ancient Goddess of Sin. It's unclear if she even knows of her and how relevant she used to be to her people.

She uses a special forging technique that originated from a strange being that once inhabited the area, though she is unaware of what it truly was. She also believes humans to be inherently different than her kind, suggesting that across the ages, the Crow People had forgotten that they originated from humans. This was probably not helped by the general distrust humanity displays when dealing with creatures who are different than them.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: Although the lower half of their bodies were transformed into a chaos spider, Quelaag and her sister managed to carve out a domain for themselves on the edge of the realm of Izalith, near what was called Blighttown. While the older Quelaag maintained control over their refuge thanks to her strength, the younger one, who was a Fire Keeper with an immense amount of humanity within her, began producing eggs by the dozen, until they covered their entire lair. In time, the Undead exiled to the depths of the Undead Burg and who had ended up in the rotten Blighttown chose to serve the Flame of Chaos and the two demonic daughters of Izalith of their own free will.

title: Mask of Judgment
snippet:
Mask of Judgment -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : A mask honoring an ancient goddess. Sin was said to be her domain, but the name of this goddess is long forgotten.

Little is known about what purpose the mask served, only that it was worn by a person of great authority.

title: Dungeon Cell Key
snippet:
Dungeon Cell Key -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Key to the dungeon of the Undead Asylum to the North.

A mysterious knight, without saying a word, shoved a corpse down into the cell, and on its person was this key. Who was this knight? And what was his purpose? There may be no answer, but one must still forge ahead.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet: At some point, after Gwyndolin had become the "Chief Deity" of the Anor Londo clan, Yorshka reached Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, the city her brother had built on the ruins of Anor Londo to house the Irithyllians, hybrids between the race of the gods of Anor Londo and humans. Here she was welcomed by Gwyndolin who formed a relationship of deep affection with his newfound sister, giving her a sacred chime and even the name Yorshka. Eventually a church was built in her name inside Irithyll—exactly where the Painted World of Ariamis was once kept— in which she was venerated as a goddess by the humans who worked in the city.

title: Greirat's Ashes
snippet:
Greirat's Ashes -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : Give to the Shrine Handmaid to expand her inventory to include items that Greirat was selling upon death, as well as what his next pillaging journey would have yielded.

title: Lothric
snippet: Due to the danger that her new faith posed to the kingdom, and despite her close position to the Queen, Gertrude was imprisoned in the ceiling cell inside the Grand Archives. Here she was subjected to the experiments of scholars, who even toyed with her sacred chime, using crystals to make a catalyst that was suitable for casting both miracles and sorceries. Eventually the abuses of the scholars led the maiden to lose both her voice and her sight, but she remained determined to write down the story of the Angel, even if in the form of incoherent scrawls.

title: Gertrude
snippet: Due to the danger that her new faith posed to the kingdom, and despite her close position to the Queen, Gertrude was imprisoned in the ceiling cell inside the Grand Archives. Here she was subjected to the experiments of scholars, who also toyed with her sacred chime, using the power of crystals to make a catalyst that was suitable for casting both miracles and sorceries. Eventually the abuses of the scholars led Gertrude to lose her voice and her sight, but she remained determined to write down the story of the Angel, even if in the form of incoherent scrawls.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Lucatiel of Mirrah -  Dark Souls II - character - trivia 
 trivia : Lucatiel's summon sign appears even if she has disappeared from the game.
In her concept artwork, it was revealed that Lucatiel's original weapon of choice was a thrusting sword similar to Chancellor Wellager's Espada Ropera.
Initially, when the first renders and screenshots of Lucatiel were revealed, many fans believed Lucatiel to be male. Her actual gender wasn't known until her voice was heard in-game.
Despite her weapon being classified as a Greatsword, Lucatiel wields her weapon like a straight sword.
Director Yui Tanimura revealed in an interview that Lucatiel was supposed to be a Don Quixote-like character and used to be accompanied by the Bell Keeper of Alken who originally had the role of his Sancho Panza. The idea was scrapped and the original face was repurposed as the iconic mask she now wears.

title: Princess of Venn
snippet:
Princess of Venn -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : The Princess of Venn was the heir to the throne of her kingdom. Her homeland despised the neighboring kingdom of Alken, and this feud was kept alive by both countries. Yet in spite of such deep-seated hatred, the young royal fell in love with the prince of the enemy kingdom, who himself felt the same way. Theirs was a forbidden love.

title: Gertrude
snippet:
Gertrude -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Gertrude was the holy maiden of the Queen of Lothric, who was said to be her mother. She taught her healing miracle to the knights of the kingdom, and they became part of the miracles in use in Lothric, implying that she had great influence on the Lothric army and clergy.

title: Lucatiel of Mirrah
snippet:
Lucatiel of Mirrah -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Lucatiel was born into a family of peasants in Mirrah, an unprivileged part of the society of this kingdom. In order to ensure the well-being of her family, Lucatiel and her older brother joined the army. At an early age, she and her brother took up fencing together and, eventually, Lucatiel's skills on the battlefield allowed her to become a knightess of the Order.

Although Lucatiel was a skilled combatant, she was no match for her brother. She claims that her brother was a far better swordsman than she was, as she was never able to defeat him. At some point in her life, her brother disappeared without a trace. Lucatiel thought that he might have fallen victim to the undead curse.

title: Abyss
snippet:
Abyss -  Dark Souls - location - trivia 
 trivia : Due to what was observed from Artorias, the phrase "falling into the Abyss" does not actually constitute entering it, but rather the near infinite and unconscious darkness of it seeking out lifeforms.
**This likely means that Wolnir was very much alive when he fell, which explains how he was able to teach grave wardens his pyromancy, though what exactly it really was that actually caused his death is uncertain.

title: Gods
snippet:
Gods -  Dark Souls III - character - later_gods_of_anor_londo 
 later_gods_of_anor_londo : Caitha, Goddess of Tears, who mourns the undeserving dead and the loved ones left behind. It is unclear whether she was already a Deity in the original pantheon of Anor Londo, but she was worshipped in Drangleic by the events of *Dark Souls II*, and by *Dark Souls III*, her cult is prominent in the reformed Way of White.
Yorshka, Priscilla's daughter and the younger half-sister of Gwyndolin from another father. She originated in the Painted World of Ariamis, but by the events of *Dark Souls III* has traveled to Irithyll and met her brother, who deified her and made her part of the Way of White's pantheon. It is unclear what she is the Goddess of, although she inherited Gwyndolin's rule of the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant.

title: Divine Pillars of Light
snippet:
Divine Pillars of Light -  Dark Souls III - spell - description 
 description : Miracle of Gertrude, the Heavenly Daughter.

Brings down multiple pillars of light in the vicinity.

The Queen's holy maiden Gertrude was visited by an angel, who revealed this tale to her.

Despite losing both her sight and her voice, she was determined to record the tale. Ordinary men cannot decipher her fragmentary scrawl, nor comprehend how it became the foundation of the Angelic faith of Lothric.

title: Gods
snippet:
The Dancer of the Boreal Valley, a direct descendant of Gwynevere, possibly her daughter. She was reduced to a life of servitude by Sulyvahn, becoming one of his Boreal Knights.
Gertrude, the "Heavenly Daughter", a maiden of Gwynevere when the latter was Queen of Lothric, believed to be Gwynevere daughter. Although she may not have been revered as a Goddess, she was the central figure of an "Angelic faith" once prominent in Lothric. According to her scriptures, Gertrude was visited by an Angel who imparted to her truths that contradicted the teachings of the Old Gods; because this new faith was heretical to the Way of White, Gertrude was imprisoned in the cell positioned high above the Grand Archives, where she likely died, and part of her scriptures were labelled heretical. It is unclear if the Angels spoken about in her tales are connected to the "Angel" beings born of the fermented humanity of the pilgrims of Londor.

title: Pus of Man
snippet:
Pus of Man -  Dark Souls III - enemy - lore 
 lore : The Pus of Man vaguely resemble serpents with twisting ivory horns protruding from their body at random intervals. Serpents are considered imperfect dragons and were at some point a symbol of the Undead. The dragon correlation would explain the presence of the horns, and the connection to the Undead might give a clue to the corruption's origins. The soul of Manus was a "viscous, lukewarm lump of gentle humanity". When Manus' humanity went wild, he became a raving beast and began to emanate the Dark, giving birth to the Abyss. It's possible that the Pus of Man are humanities similarly gone wild.

title: Penal Straightjacket
snippet:
Penal Straightjacket -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Straightjacket of the Lost Sinner.

A tightly cinched belt presses against the waist.
By now no one knows who this was used to punish, or for what reason.

title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet: Friede "protected" their world, even killing their own brethren who opposed her. The Painter, the "Lady" of the corvians, was imprisoned in the library of the corvian village, to prevent her from preparing the next Painted World.

title: Salaman the Master Pyromancer
snippet:
Salaman the Master Pyromancer -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Salaman was from an era two hundred years before the events that transpired in Lordran with the arrival of the Chosen Undead. He was the first to meet Quelana of Izalith after her self-imposed exile from her homeland. He was capable of seeing her and was thus allowed to learn her pyromancy, becoming Master Pyromancer in the world of men.

He also came to be known by the title "Great Fireball", referring to the pyromancy of the same name which he ostensibly used often, learned from Quelana herself. He would later pass on his knowledge to his own pupil, Carmina, who pushed pyromancy towards a new direction.

title: Penal Skirt
snippet:
Penal Skirt -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Skirt worn by the Lost Sinner

A tattered skirt that the guilty wear in shame.
By now no one knows who this was used to punish, or for what reason.

title: Gods
snippet:
Pontiff Sulyvahn, a cleric born in another Painted World and who later came to Anor Londo, where he would forcefully take control of Irithyll from Gwyndolin, becoming its tyrannical ruler.
King Oceiros, the King of Lothric who married Gwynevere. It is unknown what his original species was, but he would later become similar to a hybrid in an attempt to turn into a Dragon. He is the father of at least three of Gwynevere's children: Lorian, Lothric (named after the kingdom) and her youngest, Ocelotte, none of whom were deified; it is unclear whether or not he fathered Rosaria, the Dancer of the Boreal Valley, or Gertrude, but as Lorian was the heir to the throne, he was likely the two's oldest son, and perhaps their oldest child together.

title: The Duke's Dear Freja
snippet:
The Duke's Dear Freja -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : She was most likely the pet of Duke Tseldora who was fascinated by spiders. In Lord's Private Chamber the player can find a small cage with torn hole in it, likely the place where the Duke kept her. At some point Freja become host of a mysterious entity called the Writhing Ruin that grew in power, feasting on the wealth of twisted souls found in the land. This was most likely the thing that caused her transformation into her current form.

title: Giant Lord
snippet:
Giant Lord -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : The Giant Lord is the king of all Giants. After his kingdom was invaded by King Vendrick, who was under the influence of Nashandra, the Giant Lord invaded Drangleic to avenge his losses, and to retrieve the prize that Vendrick stole from him. Possessing a will of iron, the giants laid siege to Drangleic in a war that lasted for generations, and laid waste to the once proud kingdom. Eventually the Giant Lord was defeated by an unknown hero, and the giants retreated, crossing the sea to return home. The Giant Lord himself, broken and beaten, was dragged beneath the fort where he fell, and imprisoned there.

title: Drangleic Castle
snippet:
Drangleic Castle -  Dark Souls II - location - description 
 description : Drangleic Castle was the central point and seat of power of Drangleic during the country's height. King Vendrick and his queen, Nashandra, ruled Drangleic.

title: Quelana of Izalith
snippet:
Quelana of Izalith -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls_i 
 dark_souls_i : Quelana was originally a "flame witch" who used fire sorcery. When Izalith was consumed and the demons infested the city, she fled and became the creator of pyromancy. It is unknown whether the knowledge of fire sorcery was forgotten by her or whether she created pyromancy as a safer version of it. Quelana passed on her knowledge to Salaman, who in turn passed on his knowledge of pyromancy to the people of the Great Swamp.

According to a developer interview, Quelana and the other Daughters of Chaos are a different species than humans, despite being similar in appearance. Her in-game model may not reflect her "canon" appearance, with pale, ash-colored skin, as seen in the opening cutscene and achievement art.

title: Loretta
snippet:
Loretta -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Loretta is an inhabitant of the Undead Settlement, situated below the High Wall of Lothric. She was quite aged, and was the mother of the thief Greirat. She owned a bone which held some sort of importance to her, though the specifics of it are a mystery.

She was presumably waiting for her son's return, which was delayed when he was caught and imprisoned by the guards of the High Wall. All the thief wanted was to bring her a Blue Tearstone Ring, entrusting its delivery to the Ashen One when he is rescued. But Loretta had not survived long enough to meet her son's benefactor; her body is found unceremoniously stuffed into a body bag and left hanging upside-down, a fate that befalls the many corpses of the decrepit town.

title: Chime of Want
snippet:
Chime of Want -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : Sacred chime created from the soul of Nashandra. Greatly amplifies spells.

The old one of the Abyss was reborn in death, split into miniscule fragments, and spread across the land.
The tiniest of these pieces, precisely due to its size, was the first to restore its form.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet:
Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Gwynevere is the first daughter of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and one of the deities who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire. She was worshipped by the humans as the "goddess of sunlight" and a symbol of bounty and fertility, while she was also cherished by all the other gods. As a goddess of sunlight, her miracles of Bountiful Sunlight and Soothing Sunlight were able to convey the sun's rays to heal, a blessing she granted to many warriors. She also taught her miracles to her maidens and created holy water with healing properties thanks to her light. Gwynevere was venerated in a church alongside the main cathedral of Anor Londo; the structure was also used to contain the Painted World of Ariamis, protected by the Painting Guardians.

title: The Painter
snippet: The Painter was brought to the library's attic by Sir Vilhelm, who was guarding her and the key to her chamber. Vilhelm was acting on the orders of Sister Friede, who imprisoned the Painter with Father Ariandel's help. Ariandel is suppressing the Flame of the Painting with his own blood, hence only his and Friede's death can allow the Painter to see Flame. Upon being freed from house arrest, the Painter relocates from the library to the Ariandel Chapel attic. At the attic, she's found sitting in front of a big canvas; when spoken to, she divulges her vision of the new Painting. She emphasizes that the painting will show "a cold, dark, and very gentle place", which is going to be a good home for someone.

title: Lord's Blade Ciaran
snippet:
Lord's Blade Ciaran -  Dark Souls III - character - cut_content 
 cut_content : According to [https://youtu.be/ny5B9Hxn6KA?t=56 her cut dialogue], she would have reacted to the player owning a ring that belonged to Artorias, which was stolen by "a man in a long coat", likely the shady Marvellous Chester. She would then ask them if they'd be willing to hand it over to her. This sequence was replaced by her request to to be given his soul.

A potentially ominous interaction is revealed [https://youtu.be/irlXZqq5egY?t=27s in a cut dialogue] from Hawkeye Gough. He was meant to warn the slayer of Knight Artorias about Ciaran, citing her affection for the knight. This seems to imply that the assassin may have been intended to fight players for what they did to the Abysswalker, motivated by her feelings for him. In the final game, her love for Artorias is much less pronounced, and could even be seen as simple admiration.

title: Elizabeth Mushroom
snippet:
Elizabeth Mushroom -  Dark Souls II - item - description 
 description : Specially treated dried mushroom. Creates a euphoric sensation when ingested, and restores a large amount of HP over time.

Saint Elizabeth devoted her life to helping the needy by concocting medicine and potions.

It's thought her great virtue was matched only by her sublime beauty, but who can say now?

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - rings 
 rings : Each of the Four Knights was gifted a unique ring imbued with special powers. The Chosen Undead can find them scattered throughout Lordran, and their item descriptions give minor insight into who the knights were and what they did.

title: Greirat's Ashes
snippet:
Greirat's Ashes -  Dark Souls III - item - description 
 description : Umbral ash of Greirat of the Undead Settlement. With this, the shrine handmaid will prepare new items.

Greirat was a thief who fancied himself a martyr for the poor, which is what drove him to climb the wall.

title: Black Witch Garb
snippet:
Black Witch Garb -  Dark Souls III - armor - description 
 description : The purple garb of the witch Zullie, who intended to seduce Alva the Wayfarer, but eventually became his closest supporter, spending her entire life with him.

It is said that Zullie the witch, who was never loved, nor loved another, experienced all manner of misfortune, and yet in the end, found her purpose in life.

Black Witch Wrappings -  Dark Souls III - armor - description

snippet:

 description : Hand restraints of the Lost Sinner.
Increases the power of pyromancy.

A device used to restrict use of the hands.

Effect: Raises power of pyromancies

title: Velka, Goddess of Sin
snippet:
As the Goddess of Sin, Velka would eventually spread her influence inside the Painted World of Ariamis, an artificial realm that the gods exploited as a safe to seal away dangerous artifacts, abominations, sinners and Hollows; several of Velka's artifacts and miracles can be found inside of it. Dozens of her cultist followers, humans whose appearance was twisted to that of corvids, found refuge there and potentially endeavored to protect Crossbreed Priscilla from the other gods.

Velka is able to infuse the weapons of her clerics with occult power. At one point occult-infused weaponry was used to hunt the gods and their followers and some heretical cultists even went so far as to plot to destroy the gods, an attempt that culminated in failure. The connection between the source of their dark powers and their involvement with Velka however remains uncertain.

title: Caitha, Goddess of Tears
snippet:
Caitha, Goddess of Tears -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Caitha is the goddess of tears worshipped in Drangleic and its neighboring lands, and was commonly viewed as a compassionate deity that comforted people in times of tragedy. Her tears were believed to have magical properties.

She was said to mourn the undeserving dead, shedding tears as red as blood, and those who have lost loved ones, shedding pure tears of blue, for which she earned her title. These tears of the deity were believed to be the stones set in magical rings, artifacts which shared their powers with gems that originated in Catarina and Carim.

However some believed that Caitha was in fact an evil god that guided humans towards misfortune, as her chimes enable the casting of hexes. This was a branch of dark magic rooted in both sorcery and miracles instead of the miracles typical of a god, and was therefore banned in most lands.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: As the Abyss continued to spread across the land of Oolacile, Knight Artorias arrived to halt its advance and confront Manus, as the Knight of Gwyn already had experience from fighting the Abyss and its creatures in New Londo. However, Artorias's silver pendant was stolen by Oolacile's inhabitants and hidden behind an illusory wall, depriving Artorias of protection against Manus's dark sorceries. Artorias, together with his trusted companion Sif, nevertheless faced Manus, but his strength proved insufficient to defeat the Father of the Abyss. Wounded in the battle, Artorias used his Cleansing Greatshield to form a magic barrier to protect Sif against the Dark. Artorias, his soul corrupted by the Abyss and his armor corroded, was left alone in his fight against the Abyssal creatures of Oolacile.

title: Ceaseless Discharge
snippet: Around the same time, Izalith was experimenting with her Lord Soul and the power of fire and souls and at a certain point, driven by ambition and arrogance, she tried to create a "First Flame" of her own, using her own Lord Soul as a basis to make a power similar to the primordial force that had brought life into the world. The experiment, however, was not entirely successful because the result was a Flame of Chaos, an unstable power that the witch was unable to control. Izalith herself was initially consumed by it and became a beast of chaos fire along with two of her daughters in the process transforming themselves into a "Bed of Chaos". This creature, fueled by the power of the Flame of Chaos, became a seebed for a new life form: Demons.

title: Pharis
snippet:
Pharis -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : The name of Pharis was lost in the land of Drangleic, and the once-iconic equpiment came to symbolize Evlana, Goddess of the Hunt. The goddess, however, was no god at all, but rather a skilled bow huntress who became immortalized as deity with the passing of lore, long after her demise.

title: Bastille Lord
snippet:
Bastille Lord -  Dark Souls II - character - cut_content 
 cut_content : The Bastille Lord was supposed to have a name at some point during development. It was revealed in a cut dialogue from Straid, who called him and attributed the fear of those afflicted by the curse to him, rather than to the people at large as he does in the game itself. The description of the Black Set featured in the old Network Test also mentioned that the king and Straid were brothers-in-arms, who slayed an Ancient Dragon together, and in doing so "tasted omniscence".

In the released version of the game the gifted sorcerer and the lord of the bastille have no stated connection.

title: Bow of Want
snippet:
Bow of Want -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : A bow created from the soul of Nashandra.

The old one of the Abyss was reborn in death, split into miniscule fragments, and spread across the land.

Light and Dark are two sides of the same coin, much like the soul and the curse. The beings who presented themselves to those in search of kinghood were drawn to their awesome strength.

title: Yellowfinger Heysel
snippet:
Heysel's father was the leader of the Undead Legion's acolytes. Although her father was trusted with both the Farron Hail and Great Farron Dart sorceries, both are described as being "of his daughter, Heysel, [and] refined by a Crystal Sage", indicating that they were originally provided to him by Heysel, who herself uses both sorceries. The connections between Heysel and the two Crystal Sages, who specialize in crystal magic, is unclear, although one of the Sages joined the Undead Legion, which Heysel's father was a part of.

In addition to being home to her father's Undead Legion, the Farron Keep around which Heysel gravitates is also the location of the Golden Scroll chronicling the research of the Xanthous and the location of the Antiquated Set from Oolacile.

title: Giants (Lore)
snippet: Sometime around the fall of Oolacile, Gough arrived at the kingdom in response to the uncontrollable expansion of Manus' Abyss. However, he was imprisoned by the citizens of the country in a tower sealed by powerful magic. The eye holes of his helm were packed with tree resin by those who dismissed the force of the giant as brutish, indicating racist sentiments of many towards the giants.

title: Rosabeth of Melfia
snippet:
Thankfully for her, the Bearer of the Curse would find and release her from her horrible state with a Fragrant Branch of Yore. She will be extremely grateful for their help, though greatly embarrassed due to the state of her attire. After a change of clothing provided by her benefactor, she'll move to Majula, in hopes of meeting up with her teacher there. She will begin to wonder if Carhillion hadn't simply ditched her after she first lost track of him, though in truth the old master hoped she was safe and wondered where she disappeared to.

Even should they reunite in Majula, Rosabeth will decide to practice on her own, wishing to see what she can achieve by herself.

title: Velka, Goddess of Sin
snippet:
Velka, Goddess of Sin -  Dark Souls - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : At some point, Velka's influence and her followers reached Drangleic, who began creating magical rings with the shape of crow claws around a gem attuned with different elements, artifacts that remain in the region even centuries after the collapse of Vendrick's kingdom.

In Tseldora a church was built venerating the dark goddess, depicted with her iconic Book of the Guilty and talisman. Above the building Cromwell can also be found, a man who wears the robes of her ancient pardoners and performs the ritual function of absolving humans of their sins, offering forgiveness to anyone as long as they are sincere.

Despite the presence of pardoners like Cromwell, the very name Velka was lost to time in Drangleic, even as the pardoner outfit continued to serve its intended purpose; albeit under the mere shadow of the authority it represented, not the forgotten Goddess of Sin herself who was once feared by many.

title: Azal, Sage of Forossa
snippet:
Azal, Sage of Forossa -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Azal was an accomplished sage of Forossa, one of the Northwarders who earn their title after surviving a journey of great hardship. He was exceptionally skilled as he imbued his staff with magic, granting it unique powers. This made the tool unwieldy for the inexperienced, which proved the sage's magical prowess.

What became of him is unknown, but his staff can be retrieved on a corpse in Eleum Loyce, a kingdom ruled by a Forossan champion. It's possible, then, that Azal died in the frozen city, perhaps while investigating what had happened to it.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet:
Even the name has some thematic and etymological connection to Seath, as Shira resembles the Japanese word for "white", written as "**白**" and pronounced "*shiro*", a kanji that makes up part of the Duke's title of "White Dragon", written as "**白竜**". It doesn't stop there, though, as the name also shares an impressive connection with Priscilla's, as Shira's Japanese name "**シラ**" is part of the Crossbreed's Japanese name "**プリシラ**". Priscilla's connections to Seath come from her stark white coloration and her nature as a half-dragon, as crossbreeds were something the old Paledrake was highly interested in. This would make the two half-sisters, but not full ones, as Priscilla is stated to have been born of adultery, meaning they'd have two distinct mothers.

This is all just speculation, however, to be taken with a grain of salt.

title: Obscuring Ring
snippet:
Obscuring Ring -  Dark Souls III - ring - description 
 description : Ring bestowed upon the Fingers of Rosaria, invaders who seek tongues for their goddess.

Hides the presence of the wearer when far away.

It is said that Rosaria, the mother of rebirth, was robbed of her tongue by her firstborn, and has been waiting for their return ever since.

title: Chaos (mechanic)
snippet:
Chaos (mechanic) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lore 
 lore : In the Age of Ancients, the Witch of Izalith and her Daughters of Chaos wove great and powerful firestorms. At the time, the Witch and her followers were powerful flame sorcerers who lived in the city of Izalith. Blacksmiths of the ancient city crafted powerful weapons using Chaos arts. Thus, during the earliest known ages of the world, Chaos developed its reputation as a powerful force.

Eventually, the Witch of Izalith attempted to duplicate the First Flame. What she instead produced was a twisted being of chaotic fire: the Bed of Chaos, source of all demons. Several of the Witch's daughters were transformed into chaos demons, and her son became the monstrous Ceaseless Discharge.

title: Evlana, Goddess of the Hunt
snippet:
Evlana, Goddess of the Hunt -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Evlana is the goddess of the hunt, and is part of the known pantheon of deities in Drangleic. However, Evlana was originally not a goddess at all, but rather a legendary bow huntress, known for her bravery and high skill. It was only long after her death that she was turned into a deity with the passing of lore.

Her symbol is a bit difficult to discern, though it might be depicting a bird with its wings open.

title: Emerald Herald
snippet:
Emerald Herald -  Dark Souls II - character - trivia 
 trivia : The Emerald Herald was originally featured in the first trailer for *Dark Souls II*, where she is seen overlooking Drangleic and gives a feather to the Bearer of the Curse.

title: Champion Gundyr
snippet:
Champion Gundyr -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : Gundyr was an ancient champion who was charged with linking the First Flame. For his duty he received an iron halberd which would never crumble, and was sent to the Firelink Shrine. However, here the king found himself restrained by a chain that blocked him in his path, and he fell into an abyss, getting lost in the folds of time. Gundyr drifted into a moment of time when the Firelink Shrine had no fire and ended up arriving "late" for the celebrations that awaited his fate. The Fire Keeper who was supposed to welcome her champion never met him and the ensuing tragic farce became a favorite tale of the masses of Lothric, a stain on the reputation of the realm.

title: Sir Vilhelm
snippet:
Sir Vilhelm -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Vilhelm is a hollow knight of Londor who served the Sable Church and its founding sisters, but held a much deeper loyalty and admiration for the eldest of them: Elfriede. He was certainly a skilled swordsman, as all members of the Sable Church are, yet he was considered to be particularly cold-blooded in his ways, acting akin to a brutal hangman.

Eventually, his liege would leave Londor and attempt to link the First Flame, burning to ash as a result. Her motivation for doing so is unknown, but the members of her church, including her very sister, appear to view that action as abandoning their cause and a source of great shame. Despite this, Vilhelm remained loyal to her, and would join her side again once the Unkindled were called back from their graves to slay the Lords of Cinder, who refused their duties.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: The idea that the linking of the First Flame was unnatural and that it ran contrary to the order of the world is an important concept in the *Dark Souls* series, especially as the Age of Fire is prolonged perpetually by innumerable successive individuals seeking to prevent the coming of the Age of Dark.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In Ending 2: "The End of Fire", the First Flame is snuffed out, albeit with the Fire Keeper revealing that one day "tiny flames will dance across the darkness", which suggests that the First Flame partially perseveres in the form of embers within the Lords of Cinder of the past. As these Lords will use these embers of the First Flame to exert influence the world, this Age of Dark does not spell finality for the Flame. Alternatively, the player can choose to intervene as the Fire Keeper is about to extinguish the First Flame, by killing her before the cinematic ends. In this ending, the Ashen One instead takes the First Flame for themselves while the final segment of the opening narration is heard: *"Nameless, accursed Undead, unfit even to be cinder...And so it is...that Ash seeketh embers."*

title: Age of Dark
snippet:
Age of Dark -  Dark Souls - storyline - description 
 description : In the Age of Dark, the sun itself, which is connected to the status of the First Flame, is extinguished along with the Flame, and the world is enveloped in total darkness. However, it is not necessarily an existence completely devoid of fire and illumination as it might seem, as the Dark Soul of humanity itself is capable of producing everlasting flames, even if cold and generating light sources.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: What exactly the term "Age of Dark" implies is never made explicitly clear in the games, however it is stated in the canonical *Dark Souls Trilogy Compendium* to be a time when the Light fades, a Dark Lord is heralded, and humanity dominates the world. When the protagonists are given information about the Age of Dark, it typically comes from the mouths of potentially unreliable narrators, of whom Kaathe and his counterpart, Kingseeker Frampt, are examples. Kaathe asserts that the Age of Dark is "the age of men," presumably meaning the Age of those possessing Humanity in contrast to the Age of the Gods, and also declares that Gwyn "resisted the course of nature" when he linked the Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: Following the failure of this first contingency plan, a second plan is activated: Unkindled, those who had previously tried to link the First Flame but who had failed to do so, are resurrected from their graves in the Cemetery of Ash, and tasked with placing the rebellious Lords of Cinder upon their thrones so that the First Flame might be linked once more. The Ashen One, protagonist of *Dark Souls III*, is one of these Unkindled. After the Ashen One defeats each of the Lords of Cinder and places their remains upon their respective thrones in the Firelink Shrine, the Fire Keeper removes the embers of the Lords and bestows them upon the Ashen One, making them a "true lord, fit to link the fire," and imbuing them with the power to proceed to the Kiln of the First Flame.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: According to Darkstalker Kaathe, the Chosen Undead, protagonist of *Dark Souls*, is destined to bring about the Age of Dark, as they are the descendant of the Furtive Pygmy, who possessed the Dark Soul and divided it among early humans in the form of Humanity. Should the Chosen Undead abandon the First Flame to die out after the defeat of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, they will "usher in the Age of Dark", and become the fabled "Dark Lord" of whom Kaathe speaks. It is important to note that Kaathe tells the Chosen Undead that the Age of Dark had apparently already begun shortly before Gwyn chose to link the Flame, though it was seemingly ended and replaced by the Age of Fire when the Flame was linked.

title: Age of Dark
snippet:
Age of Dark -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : The Age of Dark begins when the First Flame fades completely, thus ending the Age of Fire and the rule of the gods that gained their power from it.
Since the Flame continues to burn until it goes out naturally, the Dark Age should have arrived, as naturally, when it had exhausted its fuel.

Despite the Age of Dark being a ubiquitous concept throughout the *Dark Souls* series, it is never the "current" state of the world in any of the existing games. Each of the *Dark Souls* games takes place during a late point in the Age of Fire, a point which could theoretically lead to the beginning of the Age of Dark, but which does not do so during the normal course of gameplay, with one possible exception.
