 lore : Alvina is a white Great Feline that had lived for centuries since the early Age of Fire and is capable of human speech. At one point she became a trusted friend of Knight Artorias, one of the Four Knights of Gwyn, as well as his companion Great Grey Wolf Sif.

After Artorias' death, Alvina moved to the ruins of Oolacile, now overgrown and known as the "Darkroot Garden", where the knight had succumbed in his fight against the Abyss of Manus. Sif too had moved here after he survived the battle with Manus and inherited Artorias' divine greatsword and the magical ring that had allowed the knight to cross into the Abyss. The wolf settled in the forest where Artorias' tomb had been erected and, wielding his companion's sword in his jaws, continued to fight to guard Artorias' rest, slaughtering the numerous Undead intent on plundering the tomb of the legendary knight.

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - artorias_of_the_abyss 
 artorias_of_the_abyss : Alvina can be encountered briefly during the events of the *Artorias of the Abyss* DLC, in the Chasm of the Abyss. She cannot be interacted with, in the traditional sense, and has no dialogue.

She is found after falling through an illusory floor, and leads the player to an injured but protected Sif. Here the Chosen Undead may choose to secure the white wolf by clearing the area of humanity phantoms, receiving the Cleansing Greatshield as a gift.

Elizabeth pledges to tell future generations that Artorias defeated Manus and halted the Abyss, appearing to confirm that at least part of Artorias' legend was indeed a fabrication, though he was nevertheless a brave and extremely powerful knight.

title: Ammunition (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
***Duration**: time it takes for the projectile to despawn naturally.
***Initial Speed (Horizontal and Vertical)**: initial speed at which it moves, for aimed projectiles, the Vertical speed tends to start at 0.
***Acceleration Delay (Horizontal and Vertical)**: an amount of time the projectile can exist before changing either movement speed value.
***Speed Difference**(**Horizontal and Vertical**): the amount of speed the projectile will gain/lose, starting at the end of the Acceleration Delay and ending at the limit of their Duration.
***Maximum Speed (Horizontal and Vertical)**: the maximum speed the projectile can move at, often unused as the Speed Difference usually doesn't increase the speed past this number. In cases it is used, the projectile will accelerate as normal but stay at its maximum speed once it reaches it.
***Effective Range**: distance from where the player is where the damage starts to reduce, continuing to decrease until another limit.

title: Ammunition (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Ammunition (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - item - general_information 
 general_information : Each Ammunition type corresponds directly to a weapon class that can use them. Arrows work with Bows, Bolts work with Crossbows and Greatarrows work with Greatbows.

Ammunition must first be equipped in the menu to either one of the Arrow Slots for Arrows and Greatarrows or the Bolts Slots for Bolts. Players have two slots for each type, allowing them to choose which projectile to fire each time. The Light Attack of the weapon uses the first type, the Strong Attack of the weapon uses the second.

All Ammunition types use the Attack Rating of the weapon that fires them. Unlike Spells, which only use the corresponding damage type, all damage types that the weapon has Attack rating for or the Ammunition adds are used for calculating damage.

All Ammunition types inflict Thrust damage, allowing them to deal counter damage when using the Old Leo Ring.

title: Ammunition (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Ammunition (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - item - general_information 
 general_information : Arrows and bolts must first be equipped in the 'Equipment' screen before they can be fired. Players can select up to two arrow types and two bolt types to use. When a bow or crossbow is readied, pressing the weak attack button ( or ) will use the ammunition equipped in the first (left) slot, while pressing the strong attack button ( or ) will use the ammunition equipped in the second (right) slot.

Arrows may only be fired by bows, while bolts can only be fired by crossbows. Greatarrows, on the other hand, can only be fired by greatbows. Greatarrows may be equipped in the same slot as regular arrows.

Equipping arrows or bolts in the left equip slot while a bow or crossbow is also equipped, will cause a quiver or bolt quiver to appear on the player. Having the right slot filled but the left slot empty will not cause any quivers to appear.

title: Ammunition (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
All ammunition deals the Thrust damage type. Each type has an innate damage value that is added on to the damage value of the bow or crossbow that fires them. Some ammunition can also deal elemental damage in addition to Thrust, and Poison Arrows possess the Poison status effect. Each ammunition has its own range value, which serves to increase or decrease the effective range of the weapon.

Ammunition cannot be upgraded.
